latest_release.name: v0.1.8 🚀
latest_release.body:
## Highlights ✨

- **Exact timestamps**: comments and RCA entries show the exact date and time instead of relative times like "1d ago"
- **Unified Settings header**: every Settings tab now shares one header
- **Incident drag-and-drop fixes**: dropping alerts on another alert no longer creates an incident, the Unassigned pane actually unassigns, and added alerts are attributed to the person who added them

## Improvements ✨

* Comments and RCA entries show the exact time and date instead of "1d ago" (#1462) @idanlodzki, @claude
* Settings: one shared header for every tab (#1437) @Retsumdk
* Show Resolve before Silence in alert actions (#1461) @yenugantirahul
* Remove Delete from resolved alert row menus (#1460) @flipcyde101

## Bug Fixes 🐛

* Dropping alerts on another alert never creates an incident; the Unassigned pane unassigns; added alerts are attributed to the adder (#1459) @idanlodzki, @claude
* `DELETE` of a missing on-call team returns 404 (#1467) @DeviousCardi

## Refactoring & Cleanup 🧹

* Remove the file-wide `eslint-disable` in the retention job and add named types (#1435) @Benphemeh

---

**Thanks to our contributors:** @Benphemeh, @DeviousCardi, @flipcyde101, @idanlodzki, @Retsumdk, @yenugantirahul and @claude 🙏

detail.readme:
OpsiMate

One alert queue for all your monitoring tools.

Grafana, Datadog, Zabbix, Uptime Kuma and Google Cloud each have their own alert list. OpsiMate gives your NOC one screen: every alert, one owner, one place to say "we know, it's handled" — self-hosted, one container, no SaaS.

Get Started · Docs · Demo · Website · Report Bug

---


👆 An alert with its root cause attached, rated by the on-call engineer. Click for the live demo — no signup.

### What you get - 🚨 **One queue** — alerts from every source, deduplicated by ID, with owner, status and comments on each - 🔎 **Filter, search, group** — by severity, source, tag, team, time window; save the view as a dashboard - 🔕 **Mute policies** — scheduled or ad-hoc silences that match on any alert field, without deleting anything - 🏷️ **Enrichment rules** — add tags, links and runbooks to alerts as they arrive, by pattern - 🧠 **Root cause analysis** — your system pushes a root cause per alert via the API; operators rate it 👍/👎 and the verdict is relayed back to the sender - 📈 **Insights** — MTTR, MTTA, volume and re-fire trends, per tag, with hourly resolution on short windows - ☎️ **On-call teams** and role-based access (admin / editor / viewer)

One queue — every source, one table, one owner per alert
Insights — volume, MTTR/MTTA and re-fire trends

## Key Features ### 🚨 Alert sources Every integration is a webhook — point your tool at OpsiMate and alerts appear in the queue:

Grafana
Datadog
Zabbix
Uptime Kuma
Google Cloud
Anything else
generic webhook
Each source has a setup guide in the app (Integrations → Add) with the exact webhook URL to paste. ## Run it ### Docker — one command, nothing to clone ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpsiMate/OpsiMate/main/scripts/start-docker.sh | sh ``` On first start OpsiMate generates its own private keys, one that signs login sessions and one that encrypts stored credentials (LDAP, AI, integrations), and keeps them in `data/database/` next to the database. Nothing to set up. Back up `data/database/` as a whole: without those files, everyone is signed out and saved credentials must be entered again. Upgrading from a version that used the built-in public keys signs everyone in once more, and stored credentials move to the new key on their own. Rolling back to such a version: keep the current `docker-compose.yml`, which passes both keys to the backend and the worker (older ones do not), change only the image tags (`opsimate/backend:`), and put the two files' contents in `.env` as `ENCRYPTION_KEY=` and `JWT_SECRET=`. The older version then still reads the moved credentials and keeps everyone signed in. **Access the application:** - **Backend:** [http://localhost:3001](http://localhost:3001) - **Client:** [http://localhost:8080](http://localhost:8080) - **API reference:** [http://localhost:3001/api/docs](http://localhost:3001/api/docs) — Swagger UI with "Try it out"; the OpenAPI document is at `/api/openapi.json` (set `API_DOCS_ENABLED=false` to turn both off) - **AI assistants (MCP):** `http://localhost:3100/mcp` — the `mcp` container, a read-only [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other assistants: dashboards, alerts, comments, root causes and analytics through seven tools, read from the backend with each caller's own token. Connect with `claude mcp add --transport http opsimate http://localhost:3100/mcp --header "x-api-token: "`; Settings → AI has snippets for other clients. Don't want it? Remove the `mcp` service Existing installs: fetch the latest `docker-compose.yml` first — `scripts/start-docker.sh` keeps the one you have, and older files have no `mcp` service. The first account you register becomes the admin. ### Kubernetes A Helm chart lives in [`infrastructure/helm`](infrastructure/helm); Terraform for the surrounding infra is in [`infrastructure/terraform`](infrastructure/terraform). See the [deployment docs](https://docs.opsimate.dev/docs/getting-started/deploy). ### Volume Mounts (optional but recommended) | Volume | Purpose | Required For | | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ---------------- | | `/app/data/database` | SQLite database persistence | Backend + Worker | | `/app/data/private-keys` | SSH private keys for authentication | Backend + Worker | | `/app/config/config.yml` | Custom configuration | Backend + Worker | ### Configuration ```yaml server: port: 3001 host: "0.0.0.0" database: path: "/app/data/database/opsimate.db" security: private_keys_path: "/app/data/private-keys" # Machine-to-machine token: your monitoring tools send it as X-API-Token # when pushing alerts and root causes. Change it. api_token: "change-me" ``` `JWT_SECRET` (session signing) and `ENCRYPTION_KEY` (credentials at rest) are optional: unset, the server generates both on first start and keeps them as `jwt-secret` and `encryption-key` next to the database. Set them yourself (`openssl rand -hex 32`; `JWT_SECRET` must be at least 32 bytes) to keep them in a secret store, or when several backends do not share the database directory. Keep them out of source control and the same across restarts: a new `JWT_SECRET` signs everyone out. Moving from the generated encryption key to an `ENCRYPTION_KEY` of your own is safe (saved credentials move to it on start; keep the old `encryption-key` file until the log says `Credential key check finished: every stored credential is on the current encryption key`; with Docker Compose, use a `docker-compose.yml` that passes `ENCRYPTION_KEY` to both services, as the current one does), but replacing one `ENCRYPTION_KEY` with another makes saved credentials unreadable. A small `schema.lock` file sits next to them: the backend and the worker take turns through it when they prepare the database schema at start. It holds nothing and needs no backup. ## Contributing New here? Start with a [`good first issue`](https://github.com/OpsiMate/OpsiMate/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) — each one names the exact file and line, and a maintainer reviews within a day or two. ```bash pnpm install pnpm dev # client on :8080, server on :3001 pnpm run check # lint + prettier — run this before you push; CI runs the same pnpm test ``` Bigger areas where help is welcome: new alert sources, the incident-management work, and the AI investigation agent (see roadmap). ## Roadmap **Recently shipped** - 📈 Alert Insights — MTTR / MTTA / volume trends, hourly on short windows - 🧠 Root cause analysis via API, with operator ratings fed back to the sender - 🤖 AI-powered alert search - ⚡ Server-side query engine — the queue stays fast at 10K+ alerts **Next** - 🤖 **Built-in investigation agent** — one-click root cause that actually looks at your cluster, logs and metrics ([HolmesGPT](https://holmesgpt.dev) integration, in design) - 🔄 **Incidents** — group related alerts into a named incident with a timeline and postmortem - 📣 **Alert routing** — escalation to Slack / on-call by severity and team ## Support - **[Documentation](https://docs.opsimate.dev/)** - Comprehensive guides and API reference - **[GitHub Issues](https://github.com/opsimate/opsimate/issues)** - Bug reports and feature requests - **[Slack Community](https://join.slack.com/t/opsimate/shared_invite/zt-39bq3x6et-NrVCZzH7xuBGIXmOjJM7gA)** - Join our discussions and get help - **[Website](https://www.opsimate.dev/)** - Learn more about OpsiMate ---
